## Motivation

Partially addresses #35564 — the `minimax-m2` row, reported as *"the call is gone"*.

Reproducing it on CPU (no server, no model) showed the failure is broader than a lost call: with real token-by-token streaming the detector never recognises the tool call at all and emits the raw XML markers as user-visible content, one character at a time.

Investigating that surfaced four distinct divergences from `detect_and_parse`, all in `parse_streaming_increment`. They share the same buffer-handling code, so they are fixed together.

## Root causes

**1. A partial start token was flushed as normal text.** The buffer is emitted and cleared whenever it does not yet contain the complete `<minimax:tool_call>` marker. When the marker arrives in fragments — which is exactly what detokenized streaming produces — every fragment was emitted as content and the call was never detected. The trailing partial marker is now held back using the base class's `_ends_with_partial_token`, the same way `BaseFormatDetector` does.

**2. A call with no parameters streamed no arguments at all.** `_parse_and_stream_parameters` emits nothing when the parameter dict stays empty, and the closing-brace step is guarded by `if current_streamed:`, which is falsy in that case. The streamed arguments therefore stayed `""` while `detect_and_parse` returns `"{}"`. The empty object is now emitted explicitly.

**3. Text after the end token was silently dropped.** `</minimax:tool_call>` was never consumed: after the final `</invoke>` the detector stayed in tool-call mode looking for another `<invoke>`, so any trailing content remained in the buffer and was never returned. The end token is now consumed and tool-call mode exited.

**4. An unregistered tool name leaked its markup as content.** The remaining buffer was emitted verbatim, whereas `detect_and_parse` drops the entire invoke block. The block is now skipped instead. The warning also moved so it is logged once when the block is actually dropped, rather than on every character while the block is still incomplete.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/function_call/minimax_m2.py` — all four fixes are inside `parse_streaming_increment`.

## Tests

New `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_minimax_m2_detector.py`, registered for CPU CI (no GPU, no model load).

11 cases, each replayed under **three** chunkings (character-by-character, whole string, split in half) for 33 assertions total. Every case asserts the streamed calls equal the `detect_and_parse` result with argument types preserved, and additionally that none of `<minimax:tool_call>`, `</minimax:tool_call>`, `<invoke`, `<parameter` ever appears in the returned content.

Coverage: calls with no arguments (both a populated and an empty schema), single/multiple/integer/unicode arguments, two calls in one block, text before and after the call, plain text with no call, and an unregistered tool name.

Verified before/after on this suite: 27/33 → 33/33.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code and add unit tests
- [x] Update documentation as needed — n/a, internal parser behavior

This is a CPU-only change (no kernels, no GPU code paths) and the tests live in CPU-registered suites, so `run-ci` alone should exercise it. Would appreciate a maintainer adding the label whenever convenient.

cc @JustinTong0323 @CatherineSue @zhyncs

**Disclosure:** #35625 was opened a week before this and also fixes #35564, covering all 8 parsers including `minimax_m2`. I should have found it before opening this — apologies for the overlap.

Leaving this open only so a maintainer can pick the preferred shape:

- **#35625** — all 7 detector files plus the shared base class in one PR, one parity test file (8 test methods).
- **this PR** — `minimax_m2` only, 11 test methods replayed under 3 chunkings (33 assertions).

If #35625 is the preferred route, please close this one.

What this PR isolates, in case any of it is missing there — four distinct defects rather than one:

1. **partial start marker flushed as content.** Under real detokenization `<minimax:tool_call>` arrives in pieces. A buffer holding a prefix of the marker was emitted as normal text, so the marker was destroyed before it could ever match and the call was never detected at all. Fixed by holding back a buffer that is a prefix of the marker.
2. **`{}` never emitted** for a call with no arguments — the argument dict never changes, so no fragment is produced and the closing-brace step is skipped, leaving the streamed arguments unparseable as JSON.
3. **text after the end marker lost** — content following `</minimax:tool_call>` was dropped instead of returned.
4. **unknown tool leaked its markup** — a call naming an unregistered tool emitted its raw markup into user-visible content.

Only #2 is the same class of bug as the other parsers in this issue; #1, #3 and #4 are specific to this detector's marker handling. Happy to rebase as a test-only addition on top of #35625 if that is more useful.

Rebased onto current `main` (`13f890f6`) and re-validated on CPU:

- The implementation patch applies cleanly — no upstream drift on `minimax_m2.py` since the original submission.
- New test file: **11/11 pass** with the fix; with the fix reverted on the same base, **10/11 fail** (including `test_unicode_argument` and `test_unknown_tool_is_dropped_not_leaked`), so the tests are precise regression coverage for the streaming bugs described in the motivation.

Per the review-bot's guidance on reducing the idle-PR backlog, I'm consolidating my active set: this PR stays active; the other three fixes from the same batch (#36688 / #36692 / #36695) will be re-activated one at a time as this one progresses — #36688 in particular needs conflict resolution against recent GLM detector changes and will follow once this lands or gets review traction.

One related edge case remains in the closing-brace check at `464f1dc8` (and in #35625): braces inside JSON strings affect the raw character counts.

On current main `d62b9c24`, a declared string parameter `<parameter name="pattern">a}b</parameter>` streams `{"pattern": "a}b"` without the final object brace. The non-streaming parser returns the correct argument. This reproduces with the complete call in one increment and with separate invoke/parameter/end increments, so it does not depend on splitting the start marker. Braces in parameter names and nested string values also trigger it.

The parameter builder already uses `json.dumps` for each complete key/value and deliberately leaves the outer object open. Appending one `}` at `</invoke>` when arguments are nonempty avoids counting braces in the serialized contents. A narrow local change passed 3 tests / 52 subtests; the unchanged main had 24 failing subtests. These were real-package Linux/Python 3.12 CPU checks, not server/model tests or a full run of your PR head.

Sharing this here rather than opening another overlapping parser PR. The empty-argument branch can stay as you have it.

+"""Unit tests for MinimaxM2Detector — no server, no model loading.
+
+Focused on streaming/non-streaming equivalence: feeding the same text through
+`parse_streaming_increment` in arbitrary chunk sizes must yield the same calls
+as `detect_and_parse`, and must never leak the XML markers into the content.
+"""
+
+import json
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
+from sglang.srt.function_call.minimax_m2 import MinimaxM2Detector
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(1.0, "base-a-test-cpu")
+
+TOOL_CALL_START = "<minimax:tool_call>"
+TOOL_CALL_END = "</minimax:tool_call>"
+
+
+class TestMinimaxM2DetectorStreaming(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="get_weather",
+                    description="Get weather information",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {
+                            "city": {"type": "string"},
+                            "days": {"type": "integer"},
+                        },
+                        "required": ["city"],
+                    },
+                ),
+            ),
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="noop",
+                    description="Takes no arguments",
+                    parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+                ),
+            ),
+        ]
+
+    # ---------------- helpers ----------------
+
+    def _stream(self, text, chunks):
+        detector = MinimaxM2Detector()
+        acc, order, normal = {}, [], ""
+        for chunk in list(chunks) + ["", ""]:  # trailing flushes, as serving does
+            result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            normal += result.normal_text or ""
+            for call in result.calls:
+                if call.tool_index not in acc:
+                    acc[call.tool_index] = ["", ""]
+                    order.append(call.tool_index)
+                if call.name:
+                    acc[call.tool_index][0] = call.name
+                if call.parameters:
+                    acc[call.tool_index][1] += call.parameters
+        return [(acc[i][0], acc[i][1]) for i in order], normal
+
+    def _chunkings(self, text):
+        """Char-by-char (real detokenized streaming), whole, and split in half."""
+        return {
+            "char": list(text),
+            "whole": [text],
+            "halves": [text[: len(text) // 2], text[len(text) // 2 :]],
+        }
+
+    def assert_stream_matches_final(self, text):
+        reference = MinimaxM2Detector().detect_and_parse(text, self.tools)
+        want = [(c.name, c.parameters) for c in reference.calls]
+        want_normal = (reference.normal_text or "").strip()
+
+        for label, chunks in self._chunkings(text).items():
+            got, got_normal = self._stream(text, chunks)
+
+            self.assertEqual(
+                len(got), len(want), f"[{label}] call count differs for {text!r}"
+            )
+            for (g_name, g_args), (w_name, w_args) in zip(got, want):
+                self.assertEqual(g_name, w_name, f"[{label}] name differs")
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    json.loads(g_args) if g_args else None,
+                    json.loads(w_args) if w_args else None,
+                    f"[{label}] arguments differ for {text!r}",
+                )
+
+            # Markers must never reach user-visible content.
+            for marker in (TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_END, "<invoke", "<parameter"):
+                self.assertNotIn(
+                    marker, got_normal, f"[{label}] {marker!r} leaked into content"
+                )
+            self.assertEqual(
+                got_normal.strip(),
+                want_normal,
+                f"[{label}] normal text differs for {text!r}",
+            )
+
+    # ---------------- tests ----------------
+
+    def test_call_with_no_arguments(self):
+        # Regression: streamed args stayed empty instead of "{}", and the marker
+        # was emitted one character at a time as normal text.
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather"></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_call_with_no_arguments_empty_schema(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="noop"></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_single_string_argument(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather">'
+            f'<parameter name="city">Beijing</parameter></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_multiple_arguments(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather">'
+            f'<parameter name="city">Beijing</parameter>'
+            f'<parameter name="days">3</parameter></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_integer_argument_keeps_type(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather">'
+            f'<parameter name="days">7</parameter></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_unicode_argument(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather">'
+            f'<parameter name="city">北京</parameter></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_two_calls_in_one_block(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather"></invoke>'
+            f'<invoke name="noop"></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+    def test_normal_text_before_tool_call(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'Let me check. {TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather"></invoke>'
+            f"{TOOL_CALL_END}"
+        )
+
+    def test_normal_text_after_tool_call(self):
+        # Regression: text following the end token stayed buffered forever
+        # because the end token itself was never consumed.
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="get_weather"></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+            " Done."
+        )
+
+    def test_plain_text_without_tool_call(self):
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final("The weather is nice today.")
+
+    def test_unknown_tool_is_dropped_not_leaked(self):
+        # Regression: the invoke markup was emitted as content instead of being
+        # dropped the way detect_and_parse drops it.
+        self.assert_stream_matches_final(
+            f'{TOOL_CALL_START}<invoke name="not_registered"></invoke>{TOOL_CALL_END}'
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import unittest
+
+    unittest.main()
